Larankar: Untangle Fate with Cavalry, Gold, and Subjects

Scoring-table region: South Aelantir.

Larankar (G64) is a Taychendi campaign centred on a king driven by revenge: first bring the regional powers to heel, then drive back Ameion, and finally test whether wealth and fear can keep an empire alive beyond its founder.

Story: High | Mission tree: Short as a country, long as a continuous chain (19 direct missions, followed by an imperial continuation and succession events) | Mission-tree update: implemented in the current local version; mission file last modified 2026-07-09; first release date unconfirmed | Distinctiveness: High | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Strong, combining cavalry and subjects.

Checked 2026-10-12; the base Mod and localisation both support v1.37.5.0. Difficulty and feel are inferred from scripts and a limited sample of community posts; this was not playtested.

Identity and history

Current localisation: The country's current name is Larankar, its capital is Urvand, and its ruler is Erankar. Local history script: In 1444 it is a monarchy in northern Taychend, with Larankarha culture and the Taychendi Gods faith; Ameion is its historical rival. The opening king has the Conqueror, Strict, and Sinner traits, with 5/3/6 administrative, diplomatic, and military skill—personal ability matching the kingdom's powerful position.

Local flavour text: Erankar's family was destroyed during his childhood. He later reclaimed Urvand as a mercenary leader. In 1437, he killed the enemy king outside Nanru Nakar but still lost the battle, and then faced a rebellion at home. He pieced the kingdom back together and came to regard Ameion's conqueror Laskaris as the next prophecy he had to break. This is the opening narrative's retrospective; the complete unification promised by the missions has not yet happened.

Wiki: The offline English history recounts the Eighth Kingdom and the later Larankarha Empire, emphasising local warlords, tribute networks, and common defence against Ameion. It gives two possible early foundation dates, 1433 and 1434; this article does not choose between them as settled fact. Later imperial rule and the empire's rise and fall in the Wiki are not inevitable player outcomes, and do not establish that Larankar ruled all Taychend in 1444.

National story and campaign arc

At the heart of Erankar's story is his refusal to let others decide Taychend's fate. He opposes the foreign conqueror, but also distrusts priests who preach inevitability. Cavalry mobility, political bargains, and personal will are his weapons against prophecy. The confrontation between the Two Heroes makes the conflict explicit: an outside rule that appears peaceful and prosperous may still reduce local people to obedience. [Local flavour text]

This is not a gentle story of liberation. Erankar executes enemies and may choose to destroy cities; the prosperity he supports depends on enslaved labour. The main storyline moves from revenge against old enemies and dealing with South Rjunmarka, through appointing local proxies and governing subjects, to cities and roads, then empire and succession crisis. Defeating the foreign enemy is only the first act; the country's survival depends on managing warlords and transferring power.

Core mechanics

Local scripts: Four mechanics set the campaign's pace:

  1. Hold subjects through fear and incentives. "Forge through Fear" requires prior conquest, hiring the Orphan Band, and handling the Imashend relationship and Ameion's status. Its events support diplomatic relations and subject military strength. "Bind through Greed" requires at least two subjects that receive exemption from levies, an assigned officer, or sufficient subsidies. Qualifying subjects receive reduced liberty desire for 25 years, while each adds 0.25 corruption to the overlord. Rule has a cost; annexation cannot substitute for these relationship requirements.
  2. Enslaved labour drives highland development. The greed mission also requires two provinces producing slaves, each with 5 production and a trade or production building. For each qualifying slave province, a recurring effect adds 2 tax, 2 production, and 2 manpower to two random owned highland provinces, along with a 25-year development modifier. Growth goes to the highlands, not directly to the slave-supplying province. The modifier lowers development cost but raises local unrest and governing cost, so this is not a pure gain.
  3. Roads and cavalry logistics. "Pave the North Arc" checks trade shares in two nodes and infantry garrisons along the route; completion improves allied movement and trade power along the road. Later requirements include South Arc garrisons, trade buildings, and 35 development in Urvandel. "Expand the Herd" requires manually developing each of three livestock provinces four times and stationing two cavalry units in each. The reward provides long-term goods and manpower but consumes those cavalry units. Budget both money and monarch points for construction, and account for the cost of the required troops.
  4. The Two Heroes and dynastic succession. Driving Ameion back is not judged only by battle results; the missions also check land and ruler flags. The succession mission allows an early choice while Erankar remains ruler, with at least 1 stability, 100 legitimacy, and 60 noble influence. It also preserves a completion route after the civil war, provided devastation is low across the realm and the heir has a strong claim. Further events follow the contest between Narathya and Tesheladar. Supporting one early does not guarantee a peaceful transfer of power.

Play by phase

Early on, pursue revenge against old enemies while dealing with Nanru Nakar and the Ameion threat; reserve funds for mercenaries and subject diplomacy. Ruler-specific events make progress during Erankar's reign more rewarding narratively, but the death date in the history file is not a fixed countdown. The mission to defeat Ameion also accepts a condition where Laskaris is no longer ruler, so missing the duel does not permanently lock the route.

In midgame, turn conquest into a usable proxy network. Some missions allow the overlord and non-sovereign subjects to share holdings, while cities, trade, and herds have separate requirements. North Arc garrisons by province, gold-mine city development, subject treatment, and enslaved-labour development must be scheduled together. Rapid conquest will not advance the missions if the treasury and buildings lag behind.

In the late game, confirm the religious-reform and imperial-formation requirements before preparing for succession. Do not mistake low liberty desire for a reliable inheritance, or spend all your points before discovering that road and pastoral development remain unfinished. The pressure comes from sustained progress and coordinating many conditions, not just one major war.

Formable successor and campaign boundary

Local scripts: After reforming the Taychendi faith, a general decision can form the Taychendi Empire (J84). It also requires peace, at least 1 stability, and a regional development threshold—normally 900, or 700 with a specific flag. G64's dedicated missions allow a country that was formerly G64 to be J84, so the formed empire can retain the prequel missions and gain the shared imperial tree.

This article covers Larankar's own missions and succession story. The prestige power bar, artificery, and flying city belong to the Taychendi Empire continuation. Do not project all of J84's content back onto G64's opening state, or simply add G64's 19 missions to every mission associated with a predecessor and call that one campaign's mission count. The two national-idea sets are listed separately by Tag in the appendix; whether the new ideas are adopted still depends on the formation effect and player choice.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 profile is Expansion 91 | Autocracy 90 | Magic/Artifice direction 50 | Theme intensity 18 | Pluralism 30. Conquest, cavalry deployment, and subject networks lean toward expansion; fear, incentives, and dynastic choices support strong central authority. Local proxies retain some distinct identity, but this does not amount to universal plural rights. The country's core loop is not casting or artificery, so the direction score of 50 has little matching impact at this low intensity.

Values: Evil, 28; mixed evidence; medium confidence. Dignity 20, Public Benefit 55, Recognition of Personhood 18, and Restraint 20 produce a weighted 28.25, rounded to 28. Enslaved labour and the specific city-destruction choice reduce dignity and restraint; roads, urban restoration, and the option to prohibit further raiding provide limited positive evidence. Compared with Vyzemby (23), the Taychendi Empire (22), and Ameion (47), Larankar has room for construction and restraint, but slavery cannot be downplayed. War, monarchy, and cultural unity are not penalised in themselves. No reliable phase difference of 20 points or more was established.

Recommended for players who enjoy character-driven war stories, cavalry, subjects, and a long formable continuation. Warnings: enslaved labour is central, wars recur, missions require garrisons and buildings, and succession brings further turmoil. This is a poor fit for a relaxed development campaign or a straightforward liberation narrative.

Personality differences for major choices (v2.2; not used by production matching)

The sibling succession changes more than the ruler's name. After Narathya wins, the lords fear her and advisers wait to be called upon; after Tesheladar wins, the lords continue trying to influence and manipulate royal authority. Their rule therefore represents isolated centralisation versus a crown constrained by its lords. Supporting someone early does not mean that person ultimately wins; the profiles below do not apply to alternatives such as a ruler dying early.

Axis order: scope of ambition, concentration of power, magic–artifice, plural integration, and new order.

Applicable identity and state Five-axis scores
G64 shared baseline 88 / 90 / 50 / 30 / 70
G64, Narathya actually wins 88 / 96 / 50 / 30 / 80
G64, Tesheladar actually wins 88 / 76 / 50 / 30 / 65
Former G64, now J84, Narathya actually wins 90 / 96 / 30 / 30 / 80
Former G64, now J84, Tesheladar actually wins 90 / 76 / 30 / 30 / 65

These are two story outcomes applicable under two Tags, not four separate endings. Formed J84 retains its own shared baseline; G64's magic-or-artifice direction is not carried over.

There is also a local choice in governing the Kalavend: direct annexation has a representative profile of 88 / 94 / 50 / 30 / 70; creating a strong South Rjunaka proxy frontier state has 88 / 82 / 50 / 30 / 70. The latter does not mean nationwide democracy or abolition of slavery. The endpoints adjust only the power axis for which direct evidence exists; a smaller subject is an intermediate arrangement and does not receive a newly invented profile. Local policy can coexist with either succession outcome; the two full vectors are not averaged and every combination is not enumerated. Choices to stop raiding or destroy cities also affect values, but do not create two separate national-personality profiles.

See the conditional personality profiles for full conditions and rationale. These are interpretive scores for narrative and institutions, with medium confidence, not arithmetic conversions of event rewards. The existing v2.1 personality, value score of 28, and production matching remain unchanged.

Community experience

【Community view】A guide request dated 2024-12-17 describes repeated wars and mission friction, but its author acknowledged using console commands, so it does not establish ordinary difficulty. The author's question about an island requirement does not override current scripts either. A 2025-05-12 comparison of Ameion and Larankar praises the writing and long continuation while warning that expansion and unrest can become tiring. Neither post specifies an exact game version.

An official developer diary dated 2024-11-03 discussed Erankar, subjects, a cavalry empire, and the later succession between siblings. Its then-future release language establishes development context only; current implementation is determined from local files.

Evidence boundaries

Identity, localisation, formation, and core mechanics have current local evidence. The structured cache confirms 19 direct national missions; the random-country tool's count of about 24 includes related missions from another file and must not be treated as G64-exclusive. The offline English history has a fixed revision, while the Chinese corpus did not return a directly relevant national-history page. The historical-map research directory has not completed its review of G64's succession, so it is not used to settle the date conflict. Extreme random-development outcomes, every succession branch, and in-game difficulty remain unverified.

See the evidence page for full citations and the country JSON for the player result card and complete idea text.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Larankar (G64) — Larankar Ideas

Set ID: G64_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = G64 #Larankar
    }

Larankar Traditions

  • Cavalry recruitment cost: -15% (cavalry_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Years of separatism: -5 (years_of_nationalism; raw value -5).

1. Merialeth The Manumitter

When the skies turned dark, many fled to the fortified manors of the ancient lords past, who then used the refugees for their own benefit. In one such manor a city grew, built on a defensible cliffside and ruled over by a tyrannical lord. He forced the refugees to slave away in the gold mines of the area, for that was but the only way they could receive the food and water which the tyrant controlled.

Merialeth was one such slave who, with a band of followers, escaped into the dangerous countryside. They built up their forces, and, on one stormy night, snuck into the mansion. They sneakily took out every guard in their way, managing to reach the tyrant’s bedside unhindered. Merialeth beheaded the tyrant with a special magic blade, ending his reign.

The next day, she was proclaimed the first queen of Urvand. She freed all the slaves, earning for herself the title "The Manumitter", and set about organizing Urvand into a proper city. After 22 years of rule, she left this world, bequeathing the city to her successors. Every petty noble of Urvand claims descent from the legendary queen, but only a true descendant of Merialeth can rule Urvand.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

2. Highland Horse Riders

The Larankarha horse is stronger, tougher, and stockier than its Taychendi contemporaries. While every Larankarha city has their own special breed of Larankarha horse, Urvand’s is noted for not being particularly unique. Instead, Urvand focused on breeding and sustaining massive populations of these horses, such that entire armies of Urvand’s warriors would ride into battle on the saddle. Urvand developed a specialized logistics corps, whose primary duty was not to fight, but to supply everything these horse riders required.

  • Cavalry combat ability: +20% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.20).

3. The Final Larankarha Kingdom

When Urvand consolidated the lands of the Larankarha, it propagated a simple but effective message: Urvand is the ultimate and final kingdom of the Larankarha, and anyone that opposes this will be crushed. This was the core ideology Urvand’s rulers followed, and they even went so far as to rename their state to Larankar to better reflect this unifying ideology. As Urvand subjugated the rest of the Larankarha over the 15th century, it replaced local rulers with puppets that followed this same ideology, while cunningly using propaganda to slowly wither away the local identities of the original Larankarha.

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -15% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.15).

4. High City Of Opulence

"I started my rule with Urvand full of ramshackle tents and decaying structures, but left it an organized city built of stone and gold." - the final words of Merialeth

One of the core goals every ruler of Urvand must follow is to improve their city, in so doing following the will of Merialeth. The core powerbase of the monarch are the citizens of Urvand, who will gladly stay loyal as long as their city is invested in. Thus, the city of Urvand is a beauty full of gold and opulence, resting upon and expanding into the cliffside. On the other hand, the opulent gold is mined by slaves and criminals, whose labor is used to build the city of Urvand; the forever expanding city holds this sordid secret deep within.

  • Yearly inflation reduction: +0.1% (inflation_reduction; raw value 0.1).

5. Erankar, Defier Of Fate

From the moment Erankar took breath he defied the odds, cut free from his mother and taken by fever as a newborn. Be it his daring escape from the hands of Enlarmai after the fall of his city and the execution of his family, his tortuous years spent in the Larankarha wilderness hunting with his bare hands just to survive, the half a decade he spent working his way towards one of the fiercest mercenary bands in Taychend, or his incredible and crushing victory over Enlarmai and the resulting utter destruction of their capital. At every moment, in every crisis, Erankar the Defiant spat in the face of fate, and won.

It was this defiance – this unceasing determination and unbreakable will – that allowed Erankar to create the largest state the Larankarha had ever seen. And at the Battle of Masialendi, when it was thought that no one could even harm Laskaris the Conqueror - let alone kill him - it was this defiance that allowed Erankar to land a near mortal blow on the invader, routing his army, and saving Taychend from total Kheionai dominance. No matter the challenge Larankar faces, the descendants of Erankar will always remember the spirit of the Defiant and fight against the judgements of fate for their people’s ascendency.

  • Province warscore cost: -15% (province_warscore_cost; raw value -0.15).

6. The Hadas Katti

As outsiders march upon Taychend, many warlords fall and the people suffer, as seemingly no one can stand against them. Yet, there is one kingdom that has proven itself able to resist the foreigners: Larankar. From Erankar almost killing the seemingly invincible Laskaris, to the resistance against the Sun Elves, every Taychendi seeking to liberate their homeland knows who to turn to.

These exiled warriors who fled to Larankar joined the kingdom’s army. Known as the Hadas Katti, Blades of Despair, they helped bolster the numbers of Larankar’s armies, aiding in the kingdom’s survival in the centuries to come.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

7. Recovery Against The Odds

It is said that when Erankar visited a local oracle during his march through Kalavend, the oracle spoke of how Erankar’s realm would meet its end "under the coming of the eastern sun". Erankar, an elf infamous for his defiance and disregard of fate, dismissed this as pointless, for the sun already rose in the east.

In 1516, the Jaherian Exemplars landed in South Aelantir, planning to march into Taychend and spread the truth of Surael. They found an environment ripe for disruption, as the current king of Larankar, a descendant of Erankar the Defiant, had fallen ill and was incapable of ruling. Using this brief period of weakness, the subjugated lords of Kalavend allied themselves with the Sun Elves, and launched an uprising against Larankar.

As the Kalavendhi-Exemplar alliance marched to Urvand, Larankar’s armies resisted fiercely. The siege of Urvand lasted a year, with the Sun Elves taking the city, freeing its slaves, and razing the capital. Larankar’s empire had fallen. Yet not all hope was lost, as the alliance quickly turned on each other, giving Urvand the respite it needed to rebuild. A century passed, but eventually Urvand persevered, and could shine once more.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

Larankar Ambitions

Taychendi Empire (J84) — Taychendi Empire Ideas

Set ID: J84_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J84 #Taychend Empire
    }

Taychendi Empire Traditions

  • global_manpower_modifier: +25% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.25).

  • Missionary strength: +3% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.03).

1. On The Shoulders Of Giants

Ebenanth, Yodhan, Ultarlanbeg, Olhokar. These rulers conquered Taychend, only for their empires to crumble after their demise. The Nakari and Gophirans also conquered Taychend, and attempted to build a longer lasting empire… but in the end, they failed as well.

This is all in the past now, for Taychend is once again united under our rule. One thing is certain, however: we must not let history repeat. We stand on the shoulders of giants, whose achievements and failures shaped our present reality, and while all those that came before us failed to build a truly unified Taychend, they will serve as a lesson for our emperors and scholars.

Every mistake our forebears made will be studied in detail, every folly analyzed, every success investigated, and every achievement outdone.

  • Reform progress growth: +25% (reform_progress_growth; raw value 0.25).

2. Paths Of Ascension

Our faith in the divinity of ascended heroes has created an issue now that there is no more endemic warfare in Taychend. The easiest way for a common peasant to ascend, through combat and bravery, has been closed to them. For most this is a cause for celebration. But those with ambition will see their opportunities to ascend dwindling before their very eyes.

Thus, we have set out a new program to encourage the pursuits of less warlike occupations that give our more ambitious citizens the opportunity to become gods. Most notably, this program has led to an increase in intellectual pursuits, even among the lower classes.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. The Taychendi Spring

Ever since the ruin of Aelantir, Taychend has known nothing but warfare and chaos. For millennia and beyond, the most common way a farmer could meet his end was either on the field of battle or at the edge of a marauding soldier’s blade.

With the end of unavailing warfare came a population explosion. As new generations were raised in peace and prosperity, as new crops and farming techniques spread to Taychend by way of Cannorian traders and experts, the population boomed and grew to heights never before seen in Taychend.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.10).

  • global_regiment_cost: -10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.1).

4. An Army Of Millions

Taychend’s enormous population led to a massive excess of recruits, something high-ranking commanders quickly realised and exploited. They morphed the imperial doctrine to fit this new reality, and millions of young warriors voluntarily joined the army to be sent as garrisons or to fight upon the frontiers against the barbarians. Whenever outsiders dared to try to attack the empire, a quick mobilization of hundreds of thousands of soldiers was all it took for them to leave.

  • Land force limit modifier: +25% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.25).

5. The Tailatam System

During the waning days of the 2nd Gophiran Empire, a philosopher named Tailatam wrote a series of books detailing his thoughts on how the Taychendi empire of his day could best secure its future and end the warlord cycle. While he died before he ever saw his writings be applied to the real world, his writings would form the core of what became known as the "Tailatam System".

The Tailatam System was a form of governance practiced by the empire of Taychend. At the top of the hierarchy sits the emperor, who appoints provincial governors to the provinces. These governors can be removed at any time, and only have a term of 5 years. After every 5 years, these governors return to the capital either to be fired or to be assigned to a different province. During their meeting with the emperor, they must share bread and wine while showing utter loyalty, risking execution if they fail to do so.

Nobility was not heritable under the Tailatam system. All land was owned by the emperor, and was "rented out" to the aristocracy. Thus, the nobility were forced to stay loyal, obeying all orders of the emperor and the provincial governors. For if they disobeyed, they would lose their position immediately… along with their heads.

  • global_autonomy: -0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

  • Administrative efficiency: +5% (administrative_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

6. Cult Of The Emperors

The task of ruling an empire the size of Taychend was no small feat; it could even be considered to be of legendary proportions. Thus it was no surprise to many that upon the death of the first emperor, they were declared a god. Subsequently, all emperors were declared gods upon death and, as their statues appeared in every city, the imperial cult became widespread. With this, the common people now felt they had a connection with the royal family. This not only reduced unrest in the empire, but also encouraged the loyalty of commoners towards the king and crown.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

  • Reserves Organisation: +10% (reserves_organisation; raw value 0.1).

7. Unregulated Artificery

In the 1600s, a new, smaller kind of outsider arrived on our shores, bringing with them strange magically powered inventions. Known as "artificery", many of our leaders were quick to see this technology’s potential, especially with all the ancient, powerful relics found in Taychend. These relics, as it turned out, were very useful in the application of artificery, which was the reason these foreigners came to our land to begin with.

It was decided to invite more of these "artificers" to come to our land, where they could practice and innovate upon their inventions freely and openly, away from the watchful gaze of the Ravelian Church and the Gommo. Their only concession was that they must share with us any and all artificer inventions useful for warfare. They either agreed to our terms or were promptly returned to where they had originally fled from.

  • Land fire damage: +15% (fire_damage; raw value 0.15).

Taychendi Empire Ambitions

  • Trade efficiency: +15% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.15).
